text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision; can you tell me exactly how you were positioned in the vehicle at the time of impact?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. The patient is a 25-year-old female restrained driver involved in a rear-end collision who presents with immediate onset of right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning, which is highly suggestive of an acetabular fracture or femoral neck fracture. Given the mechanism and symptoms, I will now request imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_XRay
